purpose: Dapagliflozin is used to help control blood sugar in adults with type 2 diabetes. It is also used to protect the heart and kidneys in people with heart failure or chronic kidney disease, even if they do not have diabetes. It helps reduce the risk of serious heart and kidney problems.
how_it_works: Your kidneys normally filter your blood and send sugar back into your body. Dapagliflozin blocks a protein in your kidneys called SGLT2, which stops the kidneys from reabsorbing sugar. Instead, the extra sugar gets flushed out through your urine, which lowers your blood sugar levels and also reduces stress on your heart and kidneys.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include yeast infections (especially in women), urinary tract infections, and needing to urinate more often. You may also notice your urine smells sweeter than usual. Some people experience mild dizziness or low blood pressure, especially when standing up quickly.
warnings: Do not take this medication if you have type 1 diabetes or serious kidney problems. A rare but serious condition called diabetic ketoacidosis (a dangerous build-up of acids in the blood) can occur — call your doctor right away if you feel very nauseous, vomit, have stomach pain, feel confused, or have trouble breathing. Also watch for signs of a rare but serious genital infection called Fournier's gangrene — seek immediate help if you have pain, redness, or swelling around your genitals. Stay well hydrated and tell your doctor if you are having surgery or will not be eating, as the medication may need to be temporarily stopped.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 10 mg taken once a day by mouth, with or without food, at the same time each day. Your doctor may adjust the dose based on how well it is working and how your kidneys are functioning. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
